findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The amount calculation holds: GBP 1300 x 12 = GBP 15,600 annual rent, and 15,600 / 52 x 5 = GBP 1,500.00. The GBP 1,500 deposit in s6 equals the cap and does not exceed it, and no quoted text contradicts that. The cap applies only to covered tenancies, however, and the context gives jurisdiction as "unknown" and tenancy type as "unknown". The contract also names no jurisdiction beyond a London address, so England is not confirmed. It is not confirmed that this is an ordinary private tenancy or that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. Because these facts are unresolved, the issue stays conditional rather than dismissed. This amount-cap pass says nothing about whether the deposit is protected or the arrangement is authentic. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants
